clue.text: Those wanting worn-out horse to move getting tools?

parts.note: a screw is slang for an old, broken-down horse
people wanting a horse to move are its drivers, those who urge it on

explanation.surface: A riddle about people urging a tired old nag forward, and what they might end up holding.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: drivers of a screw (old horse) read as drivers of screws, the hand tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwdrivers are the everyday hand tools for turning screws.

clue.text: Picked out, quoted for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience gets is what it hears, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: Something noticed and then repeated so listeners can hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sighted has been spotted, picked out by the eye.

clue.text: Niger's corrupt rule

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or debased, so the letters of the country's name are put out of order

parts.note: the country name is the fodder; the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A complaint that the West African country's government is crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period or fact of ruling.

clue.text: Small vehicle moving to Newgate

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A little cart heading for Newgate, the old London prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was a notorious London prison, fitting the cart picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a modest vehicle.

clue.text: Bishop coming to such a wild party would be courageous

indicators.note: the bishop coming to the party word makes the courageous one, so that word is the courageous one with the bishop taken away

parts.note: brave means courageous
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman turning up at a riotous do would need some nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive clue: B plus the answer gives BRAVE, so the answer is BRAVE without its B.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave is a large, lively all-night dance event.

clue.text: There's very short opening for it in the bar

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mouth is an opening, as of a cave or river

explanation.surface: A pub-goer saying there is barely room for something behind the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a crossword staple for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it.
explanation.definitionFit: In a bar, 'It' is short for Italian vermouth, ordered in gin and it.

clue.text: Little fellow with old books — a performer lacking emotion

parts.note: Rob is a short form of the man's name Robert
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A small man carrying antique volumes turns out to be a cold, wooden actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that carries out tasks without feeling is a performer with no emotion.

clue.text: After short time a tree is processed to make paper

indicators.note: the shuffled tree words come after the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: processed means worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Timber is pulped into paper shortly afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like the product of the pulped tree, but it means an academic essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly paper is a formal written study, the same as a treatise.

clue.text: Newspaper designation for the rabble

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
a tag is a label or name

explanation.surface: A tabloid's label for the common mob.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag, as in ragtag and bobtail, means a disreputable crowd or riff-raff.

clue.text: Checking a complete treatment

definitions.meaning: an inspection, as in giving the car a once-over
a thorough working-over, as of a room cleaned top to bottom

explanation.surface: An inspection that is also the full works.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough check, or a thorough cleaning or beating, is both called this.

clue.text: A maiden given massage back in the old country

indicators.note: back means the assembled letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to rub is to massage

explanation.surface: A young woman treated to a back rub in her homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the massaged body part but turns the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the former name of the country now called Myanmar.

clue.text: One given 12 by a letter?

parts.note: 12 across is an agreement; a letter here is someone who lets property, so this is one who signs a lease from a landlord

explanation.surface: Someone handed a deal in a piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like correspondence but means a person who lets out property.
explanation.definitionFit: A person renting from a landlord holds a lease or rental agreement from them.

clue.text: Come down with an agreement

definitions.meaning: to catch an illness, as in catch a cold

explanation.surface: Falling ill along with signing a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: One contracts flu by catching it, and a contract is a binding deal.

clue.text: Swell girl keeping one waiting?

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
someone who keeps you waiting is late

explanation.surface: A grand young woman who is always behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' looks like an adjective meaning splendid but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to expand, as pupils widen.

clue.text: Confused female star was humiliated

parts.note: lost means bewildered or confused
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A bewildered actress was put to shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To be shamed in public and lose one's dignity is the idiom here.

clue.text: Mite in grass not moving

indicators.note: in places the mite inside the informing word

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, which in slang is to sing
a tick is a small blood-sucking mite

explanation.surface: A tiny bug sits motionless in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like the lawn but is the British slang verb for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is stuck fast or jammed is not moving.

clue.text: Company member within the law — but not without guilt?

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A firm's employee obeyed the law yet still seems guilty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being complicit means sharing in wrongdoing, so one is far from innocent.

clue.text: Pieces of music with staccato playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played around with

explanation.surface: Musical works performed in short, detached notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Toccatas are keyboard compositions showing off a player's touch and speed.

clue.text: Old-fashioned member of family dies

parts.note: passé means out of date
a son is a family member

explanation.surface: An outdated relative passes away.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: to pass on is a gentle way to say someone has died.

clue.text: Walk by the shore, as theologian looking unwell getting about

indicators.note: getting about means going round, so the pale word goes round the theologian

parts.note: pale means looking unwell
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking scholar taking a seaside stroll for his health.
explanation.definitionFit: To paddle is to wade through shallow water at the edge of the sea.

clue.text: Threaten troublemaker, the limit

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
an end is a limit or boundary

explanation.surface: Warning a mischief-maker that he really is the last straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger that looms or hangs over someone is said to impend.

clue.text: One lingering in place surrounded by animals

indicators.note: surrounded by means held inside the animals word

parts.note: deer are animals
to lay is to put or place

explanation.surface: Someone dawdling in a spot hemmed in by beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dawdles or puts things off is a procrastinator who lingers.

clue.text: A fiend troubled the Church, showing bold opposition

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A devil harassing the Church of England, standing up to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Open, bold resistance to authority is defiance.

clue.text: Notice the German, a poisonous type

parts.note: an ad is a public notice
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A warning sign about a dangerous German.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake.

clue.text: Comprehensive girl having sort of ball inside

indicators.note: inside puts the ball word within the girl word

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a lob is a high, looping ball in tennis or cricket

explanation.surface: A pupil at a comprehensive school with a ball tucked inside her bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' suggests the British state secondary school, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide and all-embracing is wholly inclusive.

clue.text: Consecrate good queen, having introduced oil finally

indicators.note: the queen takes in a letter, holding it inside her name

parts.note: Good Queen Bess was a popular name for Elizabeth I

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of oil

explanation.surface: A monarch anoints something holy with a drop of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless is to make holy by a religious rite.

clue.text: Hard measure creates uproar

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A harsh punishment causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: As in all hell broke loose, the word means chaos and noise.

clue.text: Oxford may be so reprimanded

definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a style of shoe tied with strings
scolded severely, as in laid into someone

explanation.surface: The university town, or a student there, getting a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university, but here it is a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford shoes are tied up with strings, and to lace into someone is to scold them.

clue.text: Attempt to capture soldiers joining a guerrilla in perfidious conduct

indicators.note: to capture means to hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
Che Guevara was a famous guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: Troops linking up with a rebel fighter is a betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal of trust, the very definition of faithless behaviour.

clue.text: Priest sorely disposed to be wooer of those of another faith

definitions.text: wooer of those of another faith

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A clergyman much inclined to court followers of other religions.
explanation.definitionFit: A proselytiser tries to convert people to their own religion.
